conventions.convention: The global structure group is SU(2), not SO(3). The anti-Hermitian generators are T_a = −iσ_a/2, with [T_a,T_b] = ε_abc T_c and κ(X,Y) = −2 Tr₂(XY), so κ(T_a,T_b) = δ_ab.
Spacetime is R^(1,3), with metric diag(−1,1,1,1), orientation dx⁰∧dx¹∧dx²∧dx³, and increasing x⁰ time orientation. The Hodge map satisfies α∧*β = ⟨α,β⟩η volη.

Bundles have a smooth right action. When s_j = s_i g_ij, connection components transform as A_j = Ad_(g_ij⁻¹) A_i + g_ij⁻¹ dg_ij, and curvature components as F_j = Ad_(g_ij⁻¹) F_i. Curvature is F = dA + ½[A∧A].

Natural units c = ℏ = 1 are used; coordinates have length units, connection coefficients have units m⁻¹, curvature coefficients have units m⁻², and g_YM > 0 is dimensionless. The action density is −κ(F∧*F)/(2g_YM²).

Fields are smooth, there are no matter fields or current sources, and one bundle sector is selected. Stationarity uses smooth compactly supported connection variations and finite relative action differences even when the unvaried global action diverges.
The active gauge action on horizontal distributions is H ↦ dΦ(H). Its local curvature formula uses v_i determined by Φ⁻¹∘s_i = s_i v_i, giving F_i^Φ = Ad_(v_i⁻¹) F_i.
Countable choice is an explicit inherited mathematical assumption; the finite matrix calculations and Euclidean compactness argument introduce no additional choice principle.

load_bearing.statement: Adopts the smooth, source-free pure SU(2) model on oriented, time-oriented Minkowski R^(1,3), in one selected smooth right-principal bundle sector, with κ(X,Y) = −2 Tr₂(XY), fixed dimensionless g_YM > 0, action density −κ(F∧*ηF)/(2g_YM²), and compactly supported connection variations evaluated through relative action differences.

Assuming countable choice, SU(2) is compact and noncommutative; its real Lie algebra has basis T_a = −iσ_a/2 with [T_a,T_b] = ε_abc T_c, and κ(X,Y) = −2 Tr₂(XY) is positive definite, symmetric, and Ad-invariant, with κ(T_a,T_b) = δ_ab.

For the adopted smooth pure SU(2) model and compactly supported local connection variations, the connection is stationary if and only if D_Ai(*ηF_i) = 0 in every local section; these equations transform by the adjoint action on overlaps and define the global source-free equation.

Under every smooth principal-bundle gauge transformation Φ, the action density is unchanged under H ↦ dΦ(H), so every defined local action and every convergent global action are invariant. For Φ⁻¹∘s_i = s_i v_i, the transformed curvature is F_i^Φ = Ad_(v_i⁻¹)F_i. The statement additionally asserts existence of a global section over R⁴.

published_dependencies.used_for: Exact meaning of the inherited AC_omega assumption.
The real Lie-group structure of SU(2), its traceless skew-Hermitian Lie algebra, and the matrix-commutator bracket convention.
Closed and bounded subsets of Euclidean R⁸ are compact, without an additional choice assumption.
Minkowski length coordinates and dimensionless natural-action normalization; no quantum dynamics or measured coupling is imported.
Gauge transformations as smooth equivariant diffeomorphisms covering the identity.
Pushforward of horizontal distributions and covariance of vertical-valued curvature under bundle automorphisms.
Compact-support parameter differentiation, integration by parts, and the continuous-coefficient fundamental lemma in the Euler–Lagrange proof.
Smoothness and multiplicativity of the adjoint representation in overlap differentiation.
The identity d(Ad)_e(Z) = ad_Z and differentiation of varying adjoint transition maps.

concerns.concern: The Statement asserts: “Because M=R^(1,3)≅R⁴, the bundle admits a global section”. Proof steps 1.1–4.1 establish local curvature covariance and density invariance but never establish smooth triviality or existence of that section; no declared mathematical dependency supplies it. The claim is standard and is supported by [Vákár, Remark 1.1.18](https://arxiv.org/html/2110.06334), but that passage itself invokes bundle triviality from contractibility. The complete claimed theorem needs an exact adequate mathematical supplier or a local smooth-trivialization argument, including its hypotheses and choice scope. This concern affects the additional global-section clause, not the proved local gauge-invariance calculation.

Proof step 5.1 says to “use the path g_ij exp(tZ) with initial tangent X”, although X belongs to the tangent space of the base overlap and the displayed path lies in SU(2). Its initial tangent is dg_ij(X) = dL_(g_ij) Z. The derivative identity that follows is correct after this routine typing correction.

seams_checked.note: The gauge datum, principal connection, graded bracket, curvature, and associated-derivative interfaces preserve right-action signs and quotient conventions. The real adjoint derivative is obtained explicitly by complexification and restriction. The opened supplier diagrams agree with their formulas.
All three examples use F=dA+½[A∧A]. The pure-gauge example uses a section change, rather than identifying an arbitrary local map with a bundle automorphism.

The formal data and Slavnov–Taylor theorem retain the selected pure SU(2) action, coupling, units, bundle scope, and classical gauge invariance. QAP, anomaly cancellation, and regulator properties remain additional assumptions.

The Euclidean postulate reuses the SU(2) invariant-form lemma and explicitly adopts an independent Euclidean action. The sector definition expressly says the Lorentzian supplier has no Euclidean branch; no Wick-rotation deduction is attributed to it.

The inspected finite-regulator model data treat optional non-Abelian gauge data as fixed context. They do not claim that the pure Yang–Mills postulate constructs a quantum measure, supplies heavy scalar fields, or proves a continuum EFT limit.

The vector-superfield and gauge-matter interfaces preserve SU(2), κ, the right connection convention, and the bosonic gauge coefficient. Additional superfields and matter are separately specified model data.

The fundamental-matter example cites the pure-model supplier for SU(2) and the connection transition law. Its matter content comes from the separate gauge-matter model, and its displayed covariant derivative respects the supplied convention.

The N=2 and N=4 postulates preserve the normalized anti-Hermitian basis, bundle convention, coupling, and pure gauge coefficient. Extended field content and supersymmetry invariance are adopted separately.
The noncommuting scalar-potential example uses κ(T₃,T₃)=1 faithfully; its scalar potential is supplied by the N=4 model rather than attributed to pure Yang–Mills.

The independently adopted pure N=2 ultraviolet model retains the connection convention and bosonic Yang–Mills density. Supersymmetry and subsequent effective-solution inputs are not presented as consequences of the pure classical supplier.

The static adjoint-Higgs sector and its results reuse the mathematical SU(2) basis and positive invariant form. Higgs fields, energy, and asymptotic reduction are separately specified; they are not attributed to the matter-free postulate.
The explicit monopole uses the same SU(2) commutators and κ normalization. Its field equations, flux, and energy rely on the separate adjoint-Higgs suppliers.
